jobs.title: Lead Product Manager, Innovation – New Frontiers
jobs.description:
Innovate in Kirkland
This position is based at our Innovation Labs headquarters in Kirkland, Washington. Our facility features cutting-edge technology, private research and development spaces housing groundbreaking products, and open floor plans designed to foster collaboration and creativity—all to enhance your work experience.

Your Impact
Lowe’s Innovation Labs is a specialized innovation unit that keeps Lowe’s ahead of what’s next. We explore disruptive technologies, conduct hands-on applied R&D, and help the enterprise adopt promising new capabilities with less uncertainty and friction.
As Lead Product Manager, New Frontiers, you will lead and advance the Labs’ early-stage portfolio of emerging technology opportunities. You will translate technical possibilities into customer-centered use cases, testable hypotheses, and evidence-based recommendations that help Lowe’s determine where to learn, invest, partner, scale, or stop.
You will partner with engineers, designers, researchers, and business stakeholders across areas such as Physical AI and robotics, world models, quantum computing, alternative manufacturing and construction, autonomous vehicles, and other emerging domains.

Key Responsibilities
- Define the long-term vision, strategy, and investment thesis for the New Frontiers portfolio, connecting disruptive technology shifts to meaningful customer, associate, and enterprise opportunities.
- Own discovery and product development for defined New Frontiers initiatives, connecting emerging technology shifts to meaningful customer, associate, and enterprise opportunities.
- Identify customer and business problems worth solving for DIY and Pro customers through customer research, associate feedback, market signals, and operational insight.
- Translate complex technical capabilities into clear product visions, use cases, experience principles, requirements, roadmaps, and decision-ready narratives.
- Lead structured discovery, applied R&D, and experimentation in ambiguous problem spaces; design credible tests that reduce strategic uncertainty.
- Define hypotheses, learning agendas, success criteria, and phase-appropriate outcomes for explorations, proofs of concept, pilots, and incubations.
- Partner closely with engineering and design to make informed tradeoffs among customer value, technical feasibility, operational viability, speed, and risk.
- Develop and maintain initiative-level roadmaps, OKRs, metrics, and documentation that communicate near-term learning and potential long-term value.
- Synthesize experiment results and make recommendations to iterate, invest, partner, scale, pause, or sunset opportunities.
- Build productive relationships with partners across Technology, Stores, Supply Chain, Merchandising, Digital Commerce, and other functions to accelerate learning and create paths to adoption.
- Support engagement with external partners, including startups, researchers, universities, venture firms, and technology companies.
- Navigate security, legal, architecture, governance, and operational constraints while maintaining momentum and rigor.
- Create clear executive-ready narratives, demos, and artifacts that explain what Lowe’s is learning, why it matters, and what decisions are needed.
- Contribute to strong product-management practices across Labs and provide informal mentorship to product peers.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in engineering, computer science, business, design, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience may be considered in lieu of a degree.
- 7+ years of experience across two of the following: product management, product marketing, applied engineering, software or hardware development, R&D, entrepreneurship, or business analysis.
- Demonstrated experience defining product direction, roadmaps, hypotheses, and prioritization tradeoffs in ambiguous environments.
- Experience working cross-functionally with engineering and design teams.
- Ability to translate technical concepts into clear, customer-focused product strategies, requirements, and stakeholder communications.
- Experience creating or evaluating prototypes, proofs of concept, pilots, or experiments.
- Strong customer research, market analysis, and quantitative and qualitative decision-making skills.
- Strong written, verbal, storytelling, and presentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications
- Applied engineering expertise in one or more relevant frontier domains, with Physical AI, robotics, embodied AI, computer vision, autonomous systems, or world-model development strongly preferred.
- Experience building or bringing to market hardware-software systems, robotics platforms, AI-enabled products, spatial computing experiences, advanced manufacturing technologies, or other emerging-technology solutions.
- Experience in a corporate innovation lab, startup, research organization, venture-backed company, or similarly high-ambiguity environment.
- Technical depth sufficient to engage credibly with engineers on architecture, technical constraints, system behavior, experimentation design, and scale-readiness tradeoffs.
- Experience working directly with customers, field teams, stores, job sites, or operational environments to validate real-world needs and constraints.
- Experience managing external technology partners, vendors, research collaborators, or strategic alliances.
- Advanced degree in engineering, computer science, human-computer interaction, business, or a related field.
- CSPO or comparable product-management certification.

Pay Range: $111,600.00 - $212,000.00 annually Starting rate of pay may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, position offered, location, education, training, and/or experience. For information regarding our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits .

Associate Benefits ( https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/joining-our-team )
- Working at one of the largest retail companies has its perks. We offer exceptional benefits and wellness programs for eligible full-time and part-time associates, tailored for many different lifestyles. Our benefits range from health, vision and dental insurance to paid vacation, tuition assistance and parental and family-building benefits. Plus, we offer learning and development opportunities to help our associates grow their skills and achieve their goals.
- Health, Dental and Vision insurance

- Flexible spending and health savings accounts

- Education support programs, including tuition assistance and trade skills scholarships

- Other discretionary benefits (based on eligibility) include annual bonuses, enrollment in Lowe's Employee Stock Purchase Plan and/or deferred compensation plan, and grant awards

jobs.title: Associate Product Manager - Launchpad
jobs.description:
Innovate in Charlotte

Thank you for dedicating your time and talent to Lowe’s.  We want to give you more opportunities to learn and grow, so if you find a position you’re interested in below, we encourage you to apply!

Your Impact

The Associate Product Manager assists with the process of defining product and product feature requirements and communicating those requirements to user experience (UX) and technology delivery teams. This includes using customer feedback, business strategy, data/analytics, and input from UX and technology teams to develop features that result in seamless customer experiences. With direction from more senior product management team members, this role owns the vision and success criteria for the specific feature(s) within scope of responsibility.

Launchpad Program
The tech industry is constantly evolving, creating new opportunities and challenges for businesses globally. If you’re looking to break into Tech, we’ve developed a program where you will have the opportunity to engage with tech leaders, develop your skills, and learn more about our culture while advancing your career. In this program, you will gain hands-on experience in your targeted discipline and lay the groundwork for the future of tech. If you want to make a difference in your work and community, you’ll find a home here at Lowe’s.

You must be available to start on Monday, January 25th, 2027.

This program offers experience to candidates who want to break into tech by following our program timeline below:

Orientation • 1 Week
• Learn Lowe’s policies, benefits, and business strategy
• Hands-on integration with Lowe’s culture
• Learn tech processes, systems, and operations

Bootcamp • 8 Weeks
• Fast-paced learning in targeted discipline
• Dedicated coaching with a structured curriculum
• Skills assessments
• Individual & Group Projects

Rotation 1 & 2 • 12 Months
• Rotations in different areas of Tech
• Hands-on experience & meaningful work
• Professional development

Final Placement
On completion of Launchpad, you are matched with a Tech team that best suits your interests to continue advancing your career and driving big changes with Lowe’s.
You’ll gain valuable skills and a place to connect with tech leaders, all while finding full-time job placement in this expanding industry.

Innovate in Charlotte
This opportunity is based at our on-site Tech Hub in Charlotte, North Carolina. Lowe's Tech Hub is an ultramodern work environment, complete with cutting-edge technology, collaborative workspaces, an on-site barista and Zen Garden, and other perks to enhance your work experience.

What You Will Learn
- Works with peers to understand objectives and key results (OKRs) and operates inside a well-defined scope. Supports experienced product managers to understand vision and build OKRs that are aligned with business partners.

- Works with more senior team members to review and design smaller scope features/stories, engaging in usability testing where appropriate.

- Writes clear user stories to ensure delivery of high-quality features. Maps features to user value.

- Participates in agile ceremonies and works with the team to provide clarity of expectations.

- Influences feature deliverables. Influences the backlog for engineering team priorities to support small feature delivery. Drives incorporation of customer feedback into backlog.

- Works with leads and senior managers in aligning necessary work from partners to achieve the value of the features.

- Participates in product marketing and uses it to drive deep understanding of a defined scope of features. Provides data for a defined scope of features and partners with leads and senior managers to help drive alignment.

- Seeks to provide input while partnering with leads and senior managers to define objectives and data required for analytics needed, and to develop functional and technical OKRs/metrics and create corresponding data/analytics to track the health and business impact.

- Consistently monitors health of the product for pre-determined key metrics.

- Partners with engineering to build tracking/monitoring needed to get to the data for a defined scope of features.

Minimum Qualifications
- High School Diploma or equivalent

- Completion of coursework or program focused on software development or related skills (e.g., technology related college coursework, bootcamp, certification program, coding academy)

Preferred Skills/Experience
- Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, engineering, communications, or related field

- Master's degree in a related field

- 1 year of experience in product management, project management, product design, business analysis, program management, product marketing, experimentation or related area

- Experience with a Big 4 consulting firm

- Strong financial acumen

Benefits
- 10% Associate Discount

- For information about our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit: https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits .

jobs.description:
Innovate in Charlotte

Thank you for dedicating your time and talent to Lowe’s.  We want to give you more opportunities to learn and grow, so if you find a position you’re interested in below, we encourage you to apply!

Your Impact

Lowe’s Commerce Solutions (LCS) is building a suite of enterprise retail technology products designed to help retailers modernize operations, enhance customer experience, and unlock new business opportunities through technology.

Our team brings together product leaders, architects, engineers, designers, consultants, and retail domain experts who are passionate about solving complex retail challenges through technology and innovation.

We operate at the intersection of retail, technology, and innovation, partnering with global retailers to build scalable, enterprise-grade solutions that improve operational efficiency, enhance customer experiences, and unlock new business opportunities.

The Senior Manager, Product Management, will lead product strategy and execution across multiple product domains within LCS’s retail technology portfolio. This role will drive product vision, portfolio priorities, customer engagement, commercialization strategy, and product execution while partnering closely with customers, sales, engineering, and business teams.

This role will play a critical role in shaping LCS’s commercial product strategy across areas including retail checkout, unified commerce, retail media, store intelligence, AI-powered experiences, and other emerging retail technologies.

Preferred Skills/Education

- Experience partnering with sales teams on customer engagements, solution positioning, proposals, and commercialization activities.

- Strong understanding of retail operations, omnichannel commerce, store technology, or related retail technology domains.

Innovate in Charlotte

Thank you for dedicating your time and talent to Lowe’s.  We want to give you more opportunities to learn and grow, so if you find a position you’re interested in below, we encourage you to apply!

We are hiring a Lead Product Manager – Search & Recommendations to own the product strategy and roadmap for omni-channel Search and Recommendations as part of Lowe’s Enterprise Discovery charter. This role will shape how customers find, discover, evaluate, and complete their shopping missions across Lowe’s digital and store experiences. The role will lead high-visibility customer discovery experiences spanning search relevance, personalized recommendations, basket building, and emerging AI-led discovery, with a focus on improving customer engagement and ecommerce growth. The ideal candidate brings product management experience within large-scale ecommerce and/or hands-on ownership of AI-powered customer-facing products at scale.

jobs.title: Director, Product Management - Lowe's Media Network
jobs.description:
Innovate in Charlotte

Thank you for dedicating your time and talent to Lowe’s.  We want to give you more opportunities to learn and grow, so if you find a position you’re interested in below, we encourage you to apply!

Your Impact
The Director, Product Management - Lowe's Media Network leads a product team responsible for a specific product group. Responsibilities include leading research and product development efforts as well as implementation and execution of the product group strategy. This role develops a comprehensive product strategy, maintains the roadmap and backlog, and establishes the objectives and key results (OKRs) for a specific product group. In addition, the Director develops and presents detailed business cases to senior executives and leads business reviews to ensure that the team prioritizes the right work and delivers the most customer value in the fastest time possible.

Shape the future of Retail Tech
As a Product Management leader, you’ll get the opportunity to shape the future of retail technology under the leadership of one of Forbes Top 50 CIOs. You’ll also be leading a talented team who share your passion for innovation and excellence. Our halls are filled with brilliant minds from all walks of life who have the freedom to collaborate, explore their every curiosity, and build the future.

Here, you can bring your unparalleled experience to the product domain while actively contributing to the long-term product strategy of the entire organization. With a laser focus on specific strategic product areas, you can take full ownership of the end-to-end delivery process. Leveraging your skills, you’ll be able to apply your knowledge across a diverse range of product portfolios, pushing boundaries and elevating innovation to new heights.

What You Will Do
- Set and direct product vision, strategy, and OKRs for entire product portfolio. Own the long-term two- to five-year view of product vision for the product portfolio or strategic capability.

- Influence investment choices that will yield long-term customer benefits in support of vision, including owning the annual planning for the product portfolio and representing the strategy in discussions with leadership and executive stakeholders.

- Demonstrate “customer/user” expertise within a product portfolio or strategic capability and leverage enterprise-wide resources to drive improved synergies and efficiencies across product teams.

- Coach and own the care and management of “jobs to be done” by personas for all products within the product portfolio or strategic capability.

- Identify and cultivate opportunities to drive innovation across product portfolio.

- Identify issues and blockers that may delay the launch or impede the success of products in product portfolio or strategic capability, communicate to leadership, assess alternatives to resolve, and take action on recommendation.

- Establish and audit overall product operating routines across domain to ensure product excellence.

- Coach the product team on prioritization techniques and influence peers on improving prioritization decisions for product delivery.

- Set the standard across the product team and enterprise for building usable, viable, and feasible products.

- Build frameworks and patterns across the product team for product marketing and drive the team to leverage marketing techniques to illustrate the product-market fit of the designated product domain.

- Promote data-driven decision making. Coach the product team to have right product routines focused on data to help drive roadmaps.

- Align product teams on portfolio level metrics. Audit and course correct to ensure OKRs/metrics are healthy.

- Lead a team in support of achieving the company’s mission. Manage performance and foster an inclusive environment to help associates achieve their potential.

Minimum Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in business, marketing, engineering, communications, or related field or equivalent experience

- 10 years of experience in two or more of the following: project management, product management, business analysis, program management, experimentation, or product marketing

- 6 years of experience working with technology and user experience teams to define, scope and prioritize product requirements while translating business strategy into specific product features and delivering digital products and/or experiences

- 5 years of direct team leadership experience and experience managing operational and/or project financial budgets

- 3 years of experience in an agile software environment

- Demonstrated experience working cross-functionally in a large organization with senior leadership and providing guidance and direction to cross-functional resources

Preferred Skills/Education
*We encourage you to apply even if you do not have all the preferred skills or experience.*
- Retail Media Network experience is strongly preferred

- Master’s degree in business administration or similar advanced degree or equivalent experience

- 3 years of experience leading the digital product roadmap

- Prior leadership with a top 25 omnichannel retailer

- Strong financial acumen

- Certified Scrum Product Owner

Benefits
- 401k with up to 4.25% match

- Discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan (15% discount of strike price)

- Tuition-Free Education

- 10-week Maternity/Parental Leave

- 10% Associate Discount

For information about our benefit programs and eligibility, please visit https://talent.lowes.com/us/en/benefits .
